translation.title: Diclofenac Diethylammonium Cream
translation.efficacy: This medicine is used for pain relief and anti-inflammation in traumatic inflammation of tendons, ligaments, muscles and joints (sprains, bruises, etc.), localized forms of soft-tissue rheumatism (tenosynovitis, shoulder-hand syndrome, bursitis, periarthritis, etc.), and localized forms of rheumatic diseases (osteoarthrosis of the peripheral joints and spine, etc.).
translation.usage: Apply 2 to 4 g to the affected area 3 to 4 times a day according to the size of the painful area, and rub in gently so it absorbs well.
translation.caution: Do not use this medicine if you are or have been hypersensitive to it, if you are hypersensitive to aspirin or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, if you have or have had asthma caused by aspirin or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, for infants 6 years and under, in the third trimester of pregnancy, or if you are breastfeeding. Consult a doctor or pharmacist before use if you have bronchial asthma, if you are in the first or second trimester of pregnancy, if you have difficulty conceiving or are undergoing infertility testing, if you are elderly, or for children. Do not use it on damaged skin (hemorrhagic skin diseases, eczema, infected lesions, burns, wounds), in the eyes, or on mucous membranes. Do not use it under an occlusive dressing. Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are taking loop diuretics (furosemide, etc.), thiazide diuretics, medicines that interfere with hemostasis (warfarin, etc.), antiplatelet agents (aspirin, etc.), selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors or serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors. Adverse reactions may occur - sometimes itching, redness, soreness, dermatitis (rash, eczema, eruptions, papules, contact dermatitis, swelling), skin peeling and roughness, irritation and blister formation, and rarely pigmentation; and serious skin reactions such as exfoliative dermatitis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis; if any of these occur, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist. Temporary irritation and tingling may occur on damaged skin, so use with care. Store at room temperature.
